scenes.title: Key ideas
items: Testnets are practice blockchains with free, worthless coins. Ethereum's main one is…
scenes.vo: Practice run: read every prompt, do one small swap, then revoke the approval. Connect wallet: lets a site see your address. It can't move funds by itself. Sign a message: proves you own the address (for example to log in). Read it. Some "messages" are really permissions (Lesson 1.4). Approve: gives an app permission to move a specific token. Limit the amount. Transaction: actually does something (swap, deposit) and costs gas. Testnets are practice blockchains with free, worthless coins. Ethereum's main one is Sepolia. You get test ETH from a faucet (a free giveaway site). Use testnets to practise without risk.
scenes.cap: Connect wallet: lets a site see your address. It can't move funds by itself. Sign a message: proves you own the address (e.g. to log in). Read it. Some "messages" are really permissions (Lesson 1.4). Approve: gives an app permission to move a specific token. Limit the amount. Transaction: actually does something (swap, deposit) and costs gas. Testnets are practice blockchains with free, worthless coins. Ethereum's main one is Sepolia. You get test ETH from a faucet (a free giveaway site). Use testnets to practise without risk.

scenes.title: Key ideas
items: Revoke permissions you no longer need with a tool such as revoke.cash.
Add the Sepolia test network in your wallet (most wallets have a "show test networks"…
Get free test ETH from a Sepolia faucet.
Make a test swap on a testnet version of a well-known DEX (or send test ETH to yourself).
Look up the transaction on a block explorer (Lesson 1.2).
